get.summary: Finish sign-in: sets the session cookie and redirects to where sign-in started.

302.description: Signed in, to the page sign-in started from; or refused because the person is in no WorkOS organisation, to `/sign-in?error=no_organisation` with no session

post.summary:
The invitation a link's token names: its address, organisation and whether the address has an
account, for the accept screen. A token that names no open invitation is 400 `invalid_invitation`.

Accept an invitation and sign in. The address is the invitation's own: a new account gets this
password and name, and an existing one signs in with its own password.

200.description: Signed in (`done`, with the session cookie), or the next step, with a short-lived pending cookie

400.description: `invalid_invitation`; `weak_password`: the password does not meet the policy; `invalid_password`, `invalid_name`, `invalid_return_to`, `invalid_body`

401.description: `invalid_credentials`: the existing account's password is wrong

get.summary: Start sign-in: redirects to WorkOS AuthKit.

parameters.name: return_to
parameters.description: Where to go after sign-in: a path on the web app, e.g. `/companies`. Defaults to `/`.

post.summary:
Sign out: clears the session cookie, always, and ends the WorkOS session if WorkOS answers.
It never refreshes or reissues the cookie, whatever state the session is in.

204.description: Signed out; the cookie is cleared

post.summary: Email a password reset link. The answer is the same whether or not the address has an account.

200.description: `check_email`, whether or not a link was sent

post.summary:
Set a new password with the token from a reset link. It signs nobody in: the account's existing
sessions are revoked and end at their next refresh, and the person signs in with the new password.

Email a one-time sign-in code. The answer is the same whether or not the address has an account;
a limit reached is 429 `too_many_attempts`, alike for every address.

200.description: `enter_code`, whether or not a code was sent

post.summary:
Sign in with the one-time code we emailed. A wrong code and an address with no account get the
same 401 `invalid_code`.

200.description: Signed in (`done`, with the session cookie), or the next step, with a short-lived pending cookie

post.summary: Continue a sign-in into one of the organisations the last step offered.

400.description: `invalid_sign_in`: no pending choice (start again); `invalid_organisation`: not one offered

post.summary:
Sign in with an email address and password. A wrong password and an unknown address get the
same 401 `invalid_credentials`; a limit reached gets 429 `too_many_attempts` with `Retry-After`,
alike for every address.

200.description: Signed in (`done`, with the session cookie), or the next step, with a short-lived pending cookie

403.description: `csrf`; `no_organisation` (the person is in no organisation: show the page for it, no session is set); `sign_in_unsupported`

post.summary: Continue a sign-in that waits on email verification, with the code we emailed.

400.description: `invalid_sign_in`: no pending verification (start again); `invalid_code`: not a code

401.description: `invalid_code`: wrong or expired; the step stays open

post.summary: Email the code of a pending email verification again. The step stays as it is.

Set up a company in one call: the company (the caller becomes its lead), its first project,
its stakeholders and main contact, the project's scope items and success criteria, and the plan
as tasks in order. All of it or none of it. Send an `Idempotency-Key` header: a retry with the
same key and body answers the first setup with 200 and makes nothing new.

parameters.description: 1 to 128 of `A-Za-z0-9-_`, the same for a retry

200.description: Set up earlier with this key and body: that setup, as it stands

400.description: `invalid_*` naming the part, e.g. `invalid_name`, `invalid_plan` (more than 30 steps), `invalid_criterion`, `invalid_idempotency_key`; nothing is made

409.description: `rejected_idempotency_key_reused`: this key set up something else

to Secrets Manager; a workspace installed before is replaced. A workspace is one organisation's:
another's gets 409 `rejected_slack_team_claimed` and nothing is stored.

delete.summary: Forget the organisation's Slack workspace: its channel links go and its token is deleted.

get.summary:
What needs the caller across their projects: projects with no next step, open tasks and

post.summary:
GitHub's webhook deliveries for our App. No sign-in: a delivery is used only if it is signed
with the webhook secret. A pull request opened or merged in a linked repository becomes an FDE
event, once; one older than an hour, or whose body or delivery id was seen before, is refused or
changes nothing. An installation deleted or suspended is unclaimed, and repositories removed
from one are unlinked, once GitHub confirms it.

Slack's Events API. No sign-in: a request is used only if it is signed with our signing secret
within the last five minutes. The app uninstalled or its tokens revoked forgets the workspace,
its channel links and its token; every other event is acknowledged and dropped.
